C01.text: After the weakly gated rollout returned, the first request saw a readiness failure from the candidate build.

C02.text: Users kept receiving responses while the api container was recreated.

C03.text: The rollback restored the known-good build version.

C04.text: The readiness gate held the rollout open until the candidate had finished warming up.

C05.text: The memory limit kept the api container below 512 MiB under load.

provenance.capture_environment: Docker Compose project coldline-task-3-1 on one Windows host with Docker Desktop; eight long-running containers plus the one-shot initializer; no user traffic during the rollouts.
capture_method: poe roll-forward with the supplied liveness health check still in place (R01)
poe roll-forward after the health check probed /health/ready with start_period 30s (R02)
docker compose ps --format json while the candidate was running (R04)
poe release-status after limits were declared (R05)
docker compose config --format json for the weak and repaired Compose files (R06)
limits: compose_wait_seconds and timestamps are single observations from one host, not averages.
No request was sent during the container recreate window, so nothing here shows what a user would have experienced during the swap.
No memory sample under load was taken; the limits are declared values Docker applied, not evidence of what they prevented.
Image tags name local builds on this host, not registry digests.
provenance.runtime_checkpoint: Task 3.1 reference completion: pinned images coldline-api and coldline-worker, manifest releases 3.1.0 (known_good) and 3.1.1 (candidate, 20 s readiness warm-up).
